lines.text: So my next question for you is if my
subscribers have a job interview to go
to, do you have any suggestions for them
so that they can succeed?
Yes. If you are going on a job
interview, there are a couple of things
that I think managers look for or I can
tell you what at least I look for. Uh
number one, do you have the skill sets?
Do you have the right level of
experience that we're looking for for
the job? If you're meeting with me, the
likelihood is is that you already have
the skills. The second thing that we'll
be looking for is
do you want to actually work for the
company? I want to know if you want to
work there versus you just want a job.
And so I think that passion is really
important when you're looking to apply
for a new job. So just keep that in mind
as you're as you're talking to the
hiring manager.
And then the third thing that I think is
really important is also just cultural
fit. Are you going to be a good fit with
the team that you're going to be a part
of? Are you going to be a good fit with
you know the rest of the organization?
And I think that piece is really
important especially if you know that
company has a great culture that you
want to be a part of. And so um I would
say those are the three key things that
I look for. I think it's great that you
brought up culture in a workplace.
Um, because I'm sure my subscribers
haven't heard of that word used besides
talking about, you know, different
nationalities and ethnicities. So,
that's great that you use that. Did you
go to school or did you get a college
degree to do what you're doing now?
I did get a college degree. Um, I have a
double major in Spanish literature and
in journalism and right now I am
actually not doing anything that deals
with either of those things. Um, so I
manage a team of customer success
managers and um, I did not think that I
would be in this type of role. Uh I've
had you know almost 15 years of
experience mostly in marketing and I
just recently this year changed what I
wanted to do because I was just
interested in learning something else.
Cool. What is a customer success
manager?
Yes. A customer success manager is
someone who's going to be assigned to a
new customer or client or employer uh
that joins our program and we want them
to be really successful in joining our
program. So this person will help
onboard the client. they will be the
quarterback or the face of the client.
Um, becoming their, you know, go-to
person or their best friend from a
business perspective. Um, and then they
will help share outcomes and reporting
and then try to just retain the
relationship or expand the relationship.
Do you feel like you're getting
interviewed right now
for a job?
A little bit. Yeah, I do feel like I'm
getting interviewed a little bit, but it
it's in good practice, right? I think
everybody should always be practicing
their interviewing skills so that they
can get better at it.
Yeah. I mean, I'm actually asking you
questions because I don't really know
what you do even though you're my best
friend and I know you're getting
promoted left and right. So, I can't
keep up. Um, so let's go back to you
said quarterback.
Yes. Quarterback
could be a new term for a lot of my
viewers here. So, what is a quarterback?
Yes, I would love to describe what a
quarterback is. Uh, I will tell you
maybe two different definitions of
quarterback.
Bo, and my favorite quarterback is Lamar
Jackson. That is our number one favorite
quarterback. He plays for the Ravens.
Um, but the term quarterback for how I
referenced it is the person is basically
really the main point of contact, the
person that is in the center making the
calls um and really is just sort of the
face the face of uh of the customer for
the customer um and really driving all
of the actions that are needed for that
customer to be successful.
Excellent.
And for those of you who are not
familiar with the Ravens, that is an
American football team, um, based out of
Baltimore, Maryland, where we are from.
Speaking of where we're from, obviously
we are Korean, but you were not born in
Korea. Is that right?
I was not. I was born in LA where you
are.
Yeah. And how is your Korean?
I would say my Korean is
middle tier. I can definitely have a
conversation. I can read. I can write. I
can understand probably most everything
unless you go into more technical
conversations like medical or law and

would say for the most part I'm a fairly
good Korean speaker. Um, but maybe you'd
have to ask my parents on what they
think.
And so you said that you study a you
studied abroad or No, you did study
abroad, right?
I did. I did study abroad. Yes.
How was that for you?
Uh, studying abroad was an incredible
experience. I one was able to travel to
so many different countries in Europe.
Um but the most important part that I
loved was feeling like I was part of the
culture. Uh I lived there. Um, I lived
in southern Spain in Sevilla and I, um,
one fell in love with just the people
because I was a part of a new

made my Spanish significantly better
than what it was when I got there.
That's so great that you had that
opportunity.
If you were to suggest anything for my
subscribers,
um, if they're not able to make it to
America or any English-speaking country,
what would you recommend for them to
further their um, English learning?
Yeah, if you can't, you know, go to
America or a English-speaking country, I
would say the best things that you could
do are actually watching, you know,
television shows that are speak are

like, oh, I could I can kind of
understand because I'm doing it, you

one um will help with that. I um would
also recommend trying to read books,
especially ones that um are really
popular um like Harry Potter for example
or any other series that have been
really popular. I would absolutely
recommend reading those or trying to
read them. um even if it feels hard um
you'll actually get the grasp of it
fairly quickly once you start doing
that.
I think that's a really great suggestion
to get a book that is popular that has
um you know it's it's written in every
language Harry Potter for sure. When I
was learning French, I was trying to
read this book called Little Prince. And
it was helpful that I found the audio
version. So, first I would read one page

turn on the audio to compare it to my
accent and my tone. Um, so reading is
always a good suggestion. And of course,
watch my videos.
How could someone gain confidence
while speaking English to a native
English speaker?
Yeah, I know that that can feel really
scary when you're talking to someone who
knows the language inside and out. I
remember when I was in Spain and I would
try to speak in Spanish, I was timid. I
was a little scared to really go after
it. But I think if you just be
encouraged to just speak whatever it is
that you know without feeling, you know,
embarrassed about your ability or what
level you're at will actually make you
feel more confident. And the person
that's speaking to you is going to
respect that. They're going to respect
that you're trying really hard to be
able to speak the language with you. And
I also think that, you know, they they
know that you're not a native speaker
and just you attempting to speak, you
know, confidently
uh in English will be really impressive,
I will say. And and I think they would
actually even comment and say, "Hey, I'm
so impressed by um your English speaking
just because of that, you know,
confidence, level of confidence that
you're alluding to it."
I completely agree with you. Living in
Los Angeles, I encounter
a foreign person every day where I work
at a skincare clinic. We have plenty of
clients whose
uh first language was not English. And
although they're fluent enough because
they're speaking with confidence, it
helps me to understand them better and
it makes the conversation more fun. So,
I know it's easier said than done to
say, "Oh, just have confidence when
you're speaking English to a native
English speaker, but you just have to
try it." The phrase, "It's easier said
than done." This is a common phrase that
Americans use which means that when you
say something it seems really easy but
when you try to do it it's not as easy
as how it sounds. So I hope that makes
sense but that is a very common term.
